payload.question:
## Context

Discovery-stage verification (docs/history/tsk-5zv-main-checkout-lock-release/RESEARCH.md
round 1) confirmed 6 of tsk-5zv's 7 root-cause claims against the current repo:
the release-early gap is real and unfixed in both `case 'compound'`
(bin/fgos.mjs:1601-1640, settles via `addOutcome` at :1638 with no
`releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn` call) and `case 'cleanup'` (bin/fgos.mjs:1527-1577,
settles at `moveWork(...to:'blocked')` :1559 and `moveWork(...to:'done')` :1575,
same gap at both points) — the proven tsk-45z pattern at `case 'return'`
(bin/fgos.mjs:3385,3414) is confirmed real and copyable.

But claim 6 — "approve has no retry-on-lock-held unlike take/pick" — is now
FALSE in the current repo. `approveUseCase` (src/verbs/merge/approve.mjs:119-129)
and `syncRootUseCase` (src/verbs/merge/sync-root.mjs:39-105) already wrap their
`mergeRunnerItem` calls in `withLockRetry` by default, the same pattern as
take/pick (bin/fgos.mjs:2978,3051) — inline comments there ("tsk-5k4:
withLockRetry must wrap the call that can actually throw") show this was
already fixed as separate work sometime after tsk-5zv's description was
written. The asymmetry is real, just not where the description said: it's
`promote-to-component` (bin/fgos.mjs:3495 -> src/runner/promote-engine.mjs:73)
that still calls `mergeRunnerItem` directly with zero `withLockRetry` wrapping.

## Why this matters

tsk-5zv's proposed fix step 3 ("wire approve through withLockRetry ... closing
the asymmetry") targets code that is already fixed — building it as scoped
would be wasted/no-op work, and the item's `verify` plan (still "chưa xác định")
needs to reflect the real remaining gap instead. Two scope questions need a
person's call before planning: (a) drop fix-step-3's `approve` target entirely
and retarget it at `promote-to-component`, or drop it altogether if
promote-to-component's ephemeral-worktree merge path doesn't carry the same
main-checkout-lock contention risk as approve/sync-root's main-checkout merge
path (worth a quick check before assuming it needs the identical fix); (b)
whether fix steps 1-2 (release-early in `case 'compound'`/`case 'cleanup'`,
both still genuinely missing) should ship alone as a narrower item now that
step 3's original target turned out to already be resolved.

payload.verify: chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công

payload.answer:
Scope confirmed (person decision, 2026-08-24), based on docs/history/tsk-5zv-main-checkout-lock-release/RESEARCH.md round 1:

(a) Retarget fix-step-3 from `approve` to `promote-to-component`, do not drop it. Confirmed via code read: src/runner/promote-engine.mjs:73 calls `mergeRunnerItem(ephemeral.path, memberItem, { ...lockRoot: repoRoot })` -- even though the merge itself runs in an ephemeral worktree, `lockRoot: repoRoot` means it still contends for the SAME shared main-checkout lock as approve/sync-root did before their own fix. Same risk class, needs the same fix.

(b) Keep this as ONE item, do not split. All three remaining fix points (case 'compound', case 'cleanup', promote-to-component) are the same bug class -- a settling point that doesn't release/retry the main-checkout lock -- and share one reviewer/verify surface (STR65 lock discipline). Splitting adds coordination overhead with no real risk reduction.

Revised fix scope (approve/sync-root dropped -- already fixed elsewhere, confirmed by evidence, not part of this item's remaining work):
1. case 'compound' (bin/fgos.mjs, addOutcome settling point) -- add releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn(dir, resolveWriterIdentity(dir).id), mirroring case 'return''s tsk-45z pattern.
2. case 'cleanup' (bin/fgos.mjs, both moveWork(...to:'blocked') and moveWork(...to:'done') settling points) -- same release call at both.
3. promote-engine.mjs:73 -- wrap the mergeRunnerItem call in withLockRetry, mirroring the exact `runMerge = (mergeFn) => (noWait ? mergeFn() : withLockRetry(mergeFn, { waitMs }))` pattern already proven in src/verbs/merge/approve.mjs:129 and src/verbs/merge/sync-root.mjs:105.
